text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product space E, equipped with its Borel measurable structure and volume measure dx, and every continuously Fréchet differentiable W:E→ℝ satisfying ∫E exp(−W(x)) dx<∞, let Z=∫E exp(−W(x)) dx and let μ be the normalized tilted measure dμ=Z⁻¹exp(−W(x))dx. For every real-linear partial operator D from L²(μ;ℝ) to L²(μ;E), assume D is closable and assume that, for every a∈L²(μ;ℝ) and H∈L²(μ;E), (a,H) belongs to its graph if and only if there exists a smooth compactly supported φ:E→ℝ with a=φ μ-almost everywhere and H=∇φ μ-almost everywhere. Write D̄ for the partial operator whose graph is the topological closure of the graph of D. Then, for every ε>0 and every f∈L²(μ;ℝ), there exists u∈dom(D̄) such that, for every v∈dom(D̄), ε⟨u,v⟩L²(μ;ℝ)+⟨D̄u,D̄v⟩L²(μ;E)=⟨f,v⟩L²(μ;ℝ). Let U:E→ℝ, G:E→E, and F:E→ℝ denote the measurable representative functions selected by the Lp coercions of u, D̄u, and f, respectively; the original Lp elements u, D̄u, and f are equivalence classes modulo μ-almost-everywhere equality, whereas U, G, and F are functions representing those classes. The same u additionally satisfies: (1) U and G are locally integrable with respect to dx, meaning integrable on a neighborhood of each point; (2) for every continuously Fréchet differentiable compactly supported ψ:E→ℝ and every direction h∈E, the scalar functions x↦ψ(x)⟨G(x),h⟩E and x↦U(x)dψ(x)[h] are dx-integrable, and ∫E ψ(x)⟨G(x),h⟩E dx=−∫E U(x)dψ(x)[h] dx; (3) for every smooth compactly supported ψ:E→ℝ, each of x↦exp(−W(x))U(x)ψ(x), x↦exp(−W(x))⟨G(x),∇ψ(x)⟩E, and x↦exp(−W(x))F(x)ψ(x) is dx-integrable, and ε∫E exp(−W(x))U(x)ψ(x) dx+∫E exp(−W(x))⟨G(x),∇ψ(x)⟩E dx=∫E exp(−W(x))F(x)ψ(x) dx. All displayed pointwise gradients represent the Fréchet derivative through the inner product on E. The directional identity identifies G as the distributional gradient of U with respect to unweighted volume. The theorem asserts existence with these variational and distributional properties, not an explicit uniqueness conclusion, additional classical differentiability of U, a pointwise differential equation, or quantitative estimates. Closability and the exact graph description are hypotheses, not conclusions.
